facts.text: On this date in 1920, the first commercial radio broadcast aired in Detroit — today, over 2.7 billion people still listen to radio weekly, making it the world's most-reached broadcast medium.
On August 20, 1968, Soviet tanks entered Czechoslovakia. The invasion was so swift that Prague fell before most citizens woke up.
Mongolia has more horses than people — roughly 3.5 million horses to 3.4 million humans — and nearly a third of the population still lives nomadically.
The Philippines is the only country in the world where divorce remains fully illegal for non-Muslims, affecting over 100 million people with no legal exit from marriage.
Tokyo's greater metropolitan area holds 37 million people — more than the entire population of Canada — yet its murder rate is lower than that of Zurich.
On this day in 1998, Russia defaulted on its domestic debt and devalued the ruble, triggering the collapse of Long-Term Capital Management — a hedge fund run by two Nobel laureates.
On August 20, 1988, the Iran-Iraq War ceasefire sent oil prices tumbling 10% in a single session, proving peace can be just as brutal as war for certain traders.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded in 1792 under a buttonwood tree. The first securities traded were war bonds — the United States was essentially IPO-ing itself.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2.4 trillion valuation in 2022, making it worth more than the entire GDP of France. It is the most profitable company in human history by a wide margin.
The word 'salary' comes from the Latin 'salarium' — payment in salt. Roman soldiers were sometimes paid in salt, which was scarce enough to be currency. Some debts were literally worth their salt.
On this date in 1977, Voyager 2 launched. It is now over 20 billion km from Earth, still transmitting — powered by the heat of decaying plutonium, not sunlight.
Your skeleton is not static. Every decade, your body replaces nearly all of its bone mass, atom by atom, through a process called remodeling.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
On this date in 1968, Soviet tanks entered Prague. The first signal that something was wrong reached the West via cosmic radio noise — astronomers noticed broadcast interference.
Mantis shrimp see with 16 types of color receptors. Humans have 3. Yet studies show mantis shrimp are worse at distinguishing subtle hues — more channels does not mean better vision.
On this day in 1940, Leon Trotsky was fatally struck with an ice axe in Mexico City. He survived the initial blow and fought off his attacker before dying 26 hours later.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. It accepted its first students around 1096; Tenochtitlán wasn't built until 1325.
On this day in 1968, Soviet tanks rolled into Prague. The invasion was condemned by, among others, the Communist Party of Cuba — one of the stranger diplomatic moments of the Cold War.
Woolly mammoths were still alive on Wrangel Island when the Great Pyramid of Giza was being built. The last isolated population died around 1650 BCE, well into the Bronze Age.

The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 33 years before the telephone. Alexander Bain's 'electric printing telegraph' could transmit images over wire while most of the American West was still unmapped.

Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Now cited in academic psychology papers as a genuine emotional concept.
Mamihlapinatapai: a single Yaghan word for the shared, wordless look between two people who both want something but won't initiate it. The language has one known fluent speaker left.

On this day in 1940, Winston Churchill delivered his 'Never was so much owed' speech — coining the word 'undaunted' as it entered common wartime usage. The RAF pilots it honored called themselves simply 'the Few'.

Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a longing for a home that no longer exists, or perhaps never did. It folds nostalgia, grief, and belonging into a single syllable cluster that English has never successfully replaced.

On this day in 1968, Soviet tanks entered Prague — and Czech writers immediately revived the word 'normalizace' (normalization) as bitter irony. The word became a global byword for enforced forgetting.
On this date in 2017, Bitcoin's SegWit soft fork locked in after years of bitter scaling wars — it activated August 24, but August 20 marked the final signaling threshold being crossed by miners.
On this date in 2020, Ethereum's Uniswap v2 had processed over $1B in cumulative volume, making it the first AMM to cross that mark without a single order book or custodian.
The Bitcoin genesis block contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — Satoshi embedded a Jan 3, 2009 Times headline, timestamping both the block and its political purpose.
Ethereum's EIP-1559 has burned over 4.4 million ETH since August 2021 — the fee-destruction mechanism turned ETH's monetary policy deflationary during periods of high network demand.
A single Bitcoin transaction in 2010 — Laszlo Hanyecz's 10,000 BTC pizza purchase — established the first real-world commodity price for Bitcoin: roughly $0.0025 per coin.
On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet to ImageNet — the paper that ended 50 years of hand-engineered vision features and launched the modern deep learning era.
Today in 2019, OpenAI released a staged rollout of GPT-2, citing 'misuse concerns' — a PR decision that, in retrospect, massively overstated the model's danger relative to what followed.
Training GPT-4 is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US households, spent on a single training run.
Transformers were introduced in 2017 with zero recurrence and zero convolution. The authors expected the architecture to matter mainly for translation. It replaced nearly everything else instead.

DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 predicted protein structures for virtually every known organism — around 200 million proteins — in roughly 18 months, a task structural biologists estimated would take centuries by hand.
